pattern.top_pattern: TX has a large unmapped facility bucket masking true site of care
key_driver_codes: Limb Reattachment, Hip and Femur Procedures for Multiple Significant Trauma
pattern.pattern_details: TX has a material amount of DSNP HMO spend sitting in a Not Mapped facility bucket. Higher admissions, sharply higher paid per admission, and low-volume trauma outliers suggest the true site of care or facility attribution is not reliable enough yet for policy, UM, or reimbursement action. This should be treated as a mapping and classification fix first.
pattern.why_it_matters: An unmapped facility bucket can hide the real provider, care setting, and reimbursement driver behind a large spend increase.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Correct TX facility mapping for the Not Mapped DSNP HMO bucket and audit the highest-dollar cases before changing authorization rules or provider payment strategy.
pattern.validation_reason: Facility type is unmapped, so true site-of-care and provider attribution must be confirmed before business action.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped spend increased by $7.8M on 187 more admissions and about $29.6K higher paid per admit.
A one-admission trauma case added about $104K inside the Not Mapped bucket, showing low-volume high-cost exposure within an unmapped setting.
The state-level Not Mapped block also showed about a 5.7-point increase in paid ratio.
